question.problem: A telephone exchange receives an average of $7$ calls every $5$ minutes. What is the probability that the exchange will receive at least $5$ calls in the next $5$ minutes? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that calls occur independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of calls received in the telephone exchange. Since the average rate is $7$ calls every $5$ minutes, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, the number of calls can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =7,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(7).$ 

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{7}^{x}{e}^{-7}}{x!}
$$

To compute $P(X\ge 5),$ we will use the complement:

$$
P(X\ge 5)=1-P(X<5)
$$

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<5) & =P(X\in \{0,1,2,3,4\}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4) \\  & =\frac{{7}^{0}{e}^{-7}}{0!}+\frac{{7}^{1}{e}^{-7}}{1!}+\frac{{7}^{2}{e}^{-7}}{2!}+\frac{{7}^{3}{e}^{-7}}{3!}+\frac{{7}^{4}{e}^{-7}}{4!} \\  & ≈0.173\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, the probability of receiving at least $5$ calls in the next $5$ minutes is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 5) & =1-P(X<5) \\  & ≈1-0.173 \\  & =0.827\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
